<!-- This is a pull request template, you do not need to uncomment or remove the comments, they won't show up in the PR text. -->

## Proposed changes
<!-- Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue below. -->
The objective of this PR is to migrate `lib/rocketchat.js` to Typescript, but in order to get there we need to think on a safer structure first, so we can get it done without the need of a huge PR.

The idea for this PoC is to:
1. Create `lib/rocketchat` folder
2. Create `lib/rocketchat/services/sdk.ts`
> Singleton abstraction for everything capable of communicating with the server (Example: `get` , `post` , `methodCallWrapper`, etc)
3. Create `lib/rocketchat/services`
> Dehydrate server related functions into single responsibility files (Example: `getUserInfo`)
4. Create `lib/rocketchat/index.ts` in a way that the app will make use of it (instead of the `lib/rocketchat.js`) and will keep working while we refactor functions out of it

## Issue(s)	
<!-- Link the issues being closed by or related to this PR. For example, you can use #594 if this PR closes issue number 594 -->

## How to test or reproduce
<!-- Mention how you would reproduce the bug if not mentioned on the issue page already. Also mention which screens are going to have the changes if applicable -->
Since here we are dehydrating some functions out of `rocketchat.js` we need to ensure that the ones that are using our Sdk class are working properly. There are some functions like `getRoom` and `isGroupChat` that can be tested in other test scenarios, like `getPermalinkMessage`

1. `clearCache`
   1. Go to `Settings` > `Clear local server cache` (It should clear local cache)
2. `getPermalinkMessage` (and `getRoom`)
   1. Go to a chat room (test with team, group or direct message)
   2. Get permalink for a message
   3. Check that permalink works correctly
3. `getUserInfo`
   1. Go to a chat room
   2. Tap on a user (different of yours) avatar (it should display correctly username, real name and some extra fields of the user you tapped on)
4. `isGroupChat`
   1. Direct messages should show user presence icons on rooms list and room view
   2. Group DM (DMs with multiple users) should show its own icon
5. `toggleFavorite`
   1. On rooms list, swipe a room to the left and tap `star`
   2. It should work for fav and unfav
6. Connection
   1. General connection tests
   2. Make sure you address edge cases, it was refactored
7. Multiple servers
   1. Add and delete servers
   2. Switch servers and make only one is currently active
8. Share extension
   1. General testing

Notes about next 2 tests:
-  The 2FA request is based on server response and sometimes it just doesn't ask and go straight to login (maybe it's part of their logic). If that happens, try tapping `Reset` on web first just to trigger the 2FA and then try on mobile. It worked for me.
-  Pay attention to that setting on server. It completely changes the way those requests are made and it's the easier way to understand if the new logic works.


1. 2FA with `API_Use_REST_For_DDP_Calls` *ENABLED* (Admin > General > REST API > Use REST instead of websocket for Meteor calls)
   1. Make sure your user has 2FA enabled
   2. Login and it should request 2FA
   3. Go to Settings > Security and privacy > E2E Encryption > Reset E2E Key
   4. It should request 2FA
2. 2FA with `API_Use_REST_For_DDP_Calls` *DISABLED* (Admin > General > REST API > Use REST instead of websocket for Meteor calls)
   5. Make sure your user has 2FA enabled
   6. Login and it should request 2FA
   7. Go to Settings > Security and privacy > E2E Encryption > Reset E2E Key
   8. It should request 2FA

author: edgrosvenor
body:
@SarahSibert There was an issue with this component that might exist with other components (I haven't checked). Because we were using partially calculated class names like `text-{$color}` instead of the full class name like `text-yellow-800` the classes don't end up getting preserved by purgecss when running `npm run ...`. I've done a ton of this in various places and it's caused me tons of headaches. To solve it in the alert component, where I noticed it on my current project, I reworked it so that the variables hold full class names. This meant having to add a fourth variable to each alert style for the icon, since it was a variation on the text variable.

Another solution to the problem would be to simply make sure all the possible generated class names exist in full somewhere in the text of the template, even if it's in a comment. 

After you make sure this PR doesn't break anything you're working on and that I didn't make any catastrophic mistakes, go ahead and merge it in. Then as you're continuing to work on this and other projects, keep an eye out for similar situations and correct them as you encounter them.

Thank you!

author: yaronha
body:
* support running class handlers (specify handler=`[class_name::]handler`), a special task parameter (`_init_args`) with key/values dict is used to init the class, in addition if a `context` arg is present in the `__init__()` it will be set with the run context
* support for running handlers/classes from installed packages (no need to provide code with function), specify handler/class with full path (`module.submodule.method`)
* fix bug with running `local` functions which were generated using `code_to_function()` 
* extend handlers/classes search to look in multiple modules, in graph mock server add the function code/file automatically to the searched namespaces
* re-org run tests + add tests

examples:

```python
# run a class method, the class Mycls will be initialized with myarg=9
# if Mycls.__init__() accepts a 'context' argument it will be initialized with MLRun run context
params = {"_init_args": {"myarg": 9}, "x": 5}}
fn = mlrun.code_to_function("myfunc", filename=function_path, kind="local")
run = fn.run(handler="Mycls::myhandler", params=params)

# run a lib method, e.g. convert a dict struct to a json string using 'json.dumps()'
fn = mlrun.new_function("myfunc", kind="job")
run = fn.run(handler="json.dumps", params={"obj": {"x": 99}})
assert run.output("return") == '{"x": 99}'
```

After my mm was hit with a numer of failed tx yesterday, I noticed a bad actor could spamm zigzag with wrong tx and would cause mm's to drain their funds with failed tx. Depending on the throughput, this could go quite fast.

The backend should check the nonce and amount for each order, as thouse are not checked by mm's and are fixed (each mm would perform the same check).

Nonce should be equal to committed.nonce
Amount should be less than committed.balances of that token. 

Removed line 487 -> never used.

body:
Before this change if you had `{Abor<cursor>` and triggered completion,
nothing would be found because the `{` was included in the search
string. This change special-cases a few characters (braces, parentheses)
so that they don't accidentally get included in the search term.

I think that a fix that is 100% compatible with the Unison spec would be
more involved. But this seems to handle the vast majority of uses. Also
I don't think that the Unison parser even is 100% compatible with the
Unison spec 🙂.

author: chrisliebaer
body:
These changes provide an alternative fix for poor GVN performance due to excessive hash collisions, leading to catastrophic amounts of equality checks on const nodes.

Prior to this commit, nodes with no preds shared the same hash with all other nodes of the same kind, regardless of configuration. This was done with the intent to keep the code short and under the assumption that very very few nodes from the same kind, would share the same predecessors but were configured different. This turned out to be wrong for Const and Address nodes, since they don't have any predecessors.

author: jxom
body:
## What changed (plus any additional context for devs)

After a discussion w/ @markdalgleish, it was agreed that there is a missing piece in the design system which is the concept of a vertical variant of `Columns`. This introduced the concept of a `Rows` component which is a vertical variation of `Columns`. 

However, it may be a bit confusing to have both a `Row` & `Rows` component that behave a bit differently from each other, and we realised that the `Row` & `Inline` component are very similar to eachother, though a few minor differences.

This PR is a prelude to the new `Rows` component & slims up the design system layout component surface layer by consolidating `Row` into `Inline`, to make space for a new `Rows` component.

A new prop `wrap` is added to the `Inline` component, which can be set to `false` to behave exactly like the old `Row`. If `wrap` is falsy, consumers can also optionally add a `separator`. However, if `wrap` is truthy, TypeScript tells the consumer off if a separator is supplied (as it is not available on a wrapped layout).

author: duhaime
body:
Hello! I've been loving milkdown. 

To get a little further into the code, I thought it'd be a useful pedagogical exercise for me to send the world's smallest diff to support emoji typeahead syntax with uppercase inputs. 

While writing docs with milkdown, I've often wanted to add emoji to headers. Since headers are often written in titlecase, I've found myself typing emoji with uppercase letters (:HI ... ). I think the emoji typeahead should match these strings. Just now while typing this message, I notice that Github.com's markdown parser handles uppercase emojis :) 

After I made my commit, I went to run the tests and got the following stacktrace:

```
> eslint **/{src,gh-pages,examples}/**/*.{js,ts,tsx}


Oops! Something went wrong! :(

ESLint: 8.7.0

No files matching the pattern "**/src/**/*.js" were found.
Please check for typing mistakes in the pattern.
```
So I added escaped doublequotes around the lint test glob, which permits the linter to run on Monterey. I'm happy to unstack these commits if you prefer!

There were some typing tests that failed but those should be unrelated to this diff. 

If there's anything else I can do to improve this please just say the word. Either way, thanks for this excellent work.

###### Motivation for this change

This refactors the hydra package a bit, following my refactoring of the Nix
package. Mainly it:

1. removes the attrset in default.nix, we only maintain one version of hydra
   (the unstable one) so that was unecessary complexity. I don't think we'll see
   hydra moving to a realiably stable release schedule soon, and I'm not aware
   of any users of non-unstable hydra. Happy to be proven/argued otherwise on

author: variadico
body:
Currently, we don't update the JetStream configuration in `Server.nodeToInfo`. This can cause a problem if the user doesn't explicitly configure JetStream `MaxStore` or `MaxMem`. It's a problem because some code expects `MaxStore=-1` to be resolved to a real non-negative amount of bytes. Specifically, this check fails: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/blob/main/server/jetstream_cluster.go#L3683

This is what the call stack looks like.

* `jetStreamCluster.selectPeerGroup` - returns nil because `ni.cfg.MaxStore > int64(used)` is false because `MaxStore=-1`
* `jetStream.createGroupForStream` - returns nil because `selectPeerGroup` returned nil
* `Server.jsClusteredStreamRequest` - returns "insufficient resources"

The included test fails to `js.AddStream` with the error "insufficient resources" on the main branch, but passes on this branch.

body:
Added a member function `isLexical` to ValueBase.  For now, it includes values
produced by `begin_borrow [lexical]` and `move_value [lexical]` instructions.
Eventually, it will include owned arguments as well.

Respected that member function's value to prevent RAUWing and copy
propagation's lifetime canonicalization, since both would result in altering the
value's lifetime in ways that did not respect deinit barriers.
